title: Presenting a client certificate a peer does not trust destroys signature auth: make [peer_tls.identity] per-peer
description:
Found the hard way on the live host, 2026-11-22, and reverted within the
hour. This is a trap, not a configuration mistake.

WHAT HAPPENED. Configured [peer_tls.identity] on mimi.reviewcommit.com
with a freshly minted client certificate (SAN DNS:mimi.reviewcommit.com,
EKU clientAuth, our own root). mimid loaded it, client_certificate=true.
Then, against Haven's public hub, same signed request both ways:

  signature only                -> HTTP 200, handle resolved
  signature + our client cert   -> 000, "tlsv1 alert unknown ca"

So enabling our own client certificate took a WORKING peer and made it
unreachable.

WHY. The chain is all defensible behaviour and still produces a
regression:
1. mimid presents tls.identity on EVERY connection -- peer.rs's own
   documentation says "presenting `tls.identity` as this provider's
   client certificate on every connection".
2. Haven's hub requests a client certificate (verified: exactly one
   CertificateRequest in the handshake) but does not require one.
3. Offered a certificate from a CA it does not know, Haven rejects it at
   the TLS layer with unknown_ca.
4. The handshake dies before HTTP, so the RFC 9421 signature -- the
   mechanism that works -- is never seen.

Offering an untrusted certificate is therefore strictly WORSE than
offering none. Presenting nothing leaves the peer happy to fall back to
the signature; presenting something unknown is fatal.

MIMID CHANGE PROPOSED: make the client identity per-peer, not global.
[peer_tls.identity] is one certificate for all peers, which forces an
all-or-nothing choice between "no peer can authenticate us by
certificate" and "any peer that does not trust our root becomes
unreachable". A per-peer setting -- [provider_auth.peers."<domain>"] or a
[peer_tls.peers."<domain>"] identity -- lets mimid present a certificate
only to the peers that asked for it, which is the only safe shape once
there is more than one peer. Note the symmetry: pkix_anchors is ALREADY
per-peer for the inbound direction (PeerAuthConfig.pkix_anchors), so the
outbound direction is the odd one out.

DRAFT IMPLICATION, worth raising for provider-auth -01 or -02: §7 says a
provider "MAY present a client certificate" and says nothing about the
consequence of presenting one the target does not trust. A sentence is
warranted, because the failure is silent, total, and looks like the peer
being down. Something like: a source provider SHOULD NOT present a
client certificate to a target that has not indicated it trusts the
issuer, since a target that rejects the certificate at the TLS layer
denies itself the other mechanisms. Posting needs Mark's OK.

LIVE STATE: reverted. /etc/mimid/mimid.toml carries a comment saying
[peer_tls.identity] is deliberately unset and why. The certificate and
root remain at /etc/mimid/identity/ (root fingerprint sha256
66:C6:D9:00:E4:73:97:D1:B5:8B:96:CA:56:73:DF:9B:B3:AE:08:03:81:67:48:
58:8D:5E:16:A5:5D:74:58:64), ready to turn on for a peer that confirms
it trusts that root. Haven reachable again: signed identifierQuery
returns 200.
